packages.title: Launches into walls and the curb, and launches from behind: the ragdoll takes over from the pose on screen (plus the stale first-tick ragdoll pose and the launch blends as tunables)
packages.notes:
PRIORITY 1. Two mediums: the gap review's biggest problems 1 and 3. If the window runs short, do gap-01 and gap-03 first.

OWNERSHIP
- Owns: game/actors/combat_actor.gd except blink_shown() (r2-dummy-comeback changes only its 0.5 duty), game/actors/ragdoll.gd, tests/test_ragdoll.gd and tests/test_launch_from_hold.gd.
- humanoid_rig.gd: ONLY the '# --- Ragdoll' block, ragdoll_start() through get_visual_point_transform() (about lines 531-655). New ragdoll_* functions may go there. r2-vfx-first-use owns _build_materials(), set_damage_look() and the flash_at() doc comment. r2-player-ko-view owns _apply_layers() and the first_person_body export.
- placeholder_poses.gd: ONLY launched_a() and launched_b(), plus new pose functions right after them. r2-dummy-comeback owns stagger_right_a() and stagger_right_b().
- placeholder_anims.gd: only the launched entry (about line 244).
- New animation ids: prefer none. If you add one, also add it to test_humanoid_rig.gd's id list (lines 42-43) and to ARCHITECTURE's 'Animation ids' list. Make no other edit to test_humanoid_rig.gd.
- Don't edit player.gd, first_person_camera.gd, training_dummy.gd or tests/fp_view.gd. Put any new lens helper inside test_ragdoll.gd. Never run gen_moves.gd.

SHARED ROOT CAUSE (gap-01 and gap-03, merged)
- CombatActor._launch() snaps every launch that isn't out of a hold into an animation pose with a 0.03 s blend. Any non-KNOCKDOWN reaction gets the arch-back 'launched' pose, whatever the facing.
- It calls _ragdoll_full(..., at_once = from_hold), so the full ragdoll rises from that snap over ragdoll_full_rise_s.
- Meanwhile the hips spring (Ragdoll._step(), ragdoll_hips_hz) pulls the whole body toward the animation's hips on the CharacterBody.
- Where the snap disagrees with the space around the body, the drawn body goes there first: a wall or the curb behind it puts the head 0.38 m into the wall; the attacker behind it puts the head 0.098 m from the lens over 67% of the view.
- gap-07 is in the same function. Ragdoll.start() doesn't seed the cached drawn pose, and the take-over-at-once that both fixes rely on must show and report a correct pose on its first tick.

ORDER
1) gap-01.
- Detect a launched, thrown or knocked-down body whose capsule is blocked by LAYER_WORLD: on the launch tick (a cast along the knockback) or in flight (after move_and_slide in the flying states). Detect it in the simulation, never from the ragdoll.
- Then the full ragdoll takes over at once from the pose on screen. Ragdoll.start() returns early when the mode is already FULL, so add a take-over call (HumanoidRig -> Ragdoll) that raises the influence to 1 from what shows.
- Loosen the hips pull while the capsule is stopped in flight (a new tunable in Ragdoll > 'Hips spring'). The world-colliding bodies then keep the head out of the wall, and the body slumps down or along it.
- Restore the normal pull on landing: a lying body must stay within test_ragdoll's 0.15 m (face up) and 0.2 m (face down) of its hurtboxes.
- Do steps 1 and 3 of the suggested fix ONLY. Deflecting the knockback along the wall (step 2), a wall-splat and a bounce (step 4) are new design. Leave the knockback as it is, and write the wall reaction up in 'remaining' as a question for Game-boy.
- Tests in test_ragdoll.gd: an uppercut and a haymaker 0.45 m from a wall, and one toward the curb, leave no drawn vertex more than 0.05 m inside the world. The first-person lens rules (nothing within 0.25 m, at most half the view) hold for the uppercut's launch in a corner.
- The hook stagger's fists in the corner (0.14 m from the lens, 50-59% of the view) come from a partial ragdoll, not a launch. If this fix doesn't clear them, report it in 'remaining': a magnetism change would be in player.gd, which is another package's file.
2) gap-03.
- A launch from behind (hit.from_behind, not a KNOCKDOWN) must not snap into the arch-back pose.
- Preferred: take over at once with step 1's mechanism, so the kick carries the head away from the attacker.
- Otherwise snap a forward-pitching pose: an existing one such as knockdown_forward, or the launched pose mirrored.
- Keep the face-down landing: ragdoll_aim_landing(&'downed_front') and ragdoll_bot's 'Ragdoll: uppercut from behind, lands face down'.
- Add the from-behind uppercut to a first-person lens test (nothing within 0.25 m, at most half the view). Check the shoes that sweep up through the lower view afterwards (in also_noticed) and report what you see.
3) gap-07.
- In Ragdoll.start(), when the mode goes from NONE to running, seed _visual from rig.animation_pose() and visual_rig_transform from rig.global_transform. The 'shown' pose is already read before the mode changes, so only the readers after it are stale.
- Update ragdoll.gd's header (lines 3-6) and ARCHITECTURE's Ragdoll 'Get-up' bullet (it says 'the one place the ragdoll feeds the simulation'). Both should name TrainingDummy._has_room() as the second place.
- Don't change _has_room() (r2-dummy-comeback's file).
- Test: ragdoll a dummy, move it with set_post(), and ragdoll it again. On the hit tick, get_visual_point_transform(&'Hips') is at the new body, not the old spot.
4) gap-08, part (d) only.
- Move _RELEASE_BLEND_S (0.22 s; used by release_from_grab() and by _launch() out of a hold) to a 'Grab and weapons' tunable.
- Move the 0.03 s snap blends (_launch(), guard_break at about line 850, held at about 963, the flinch at about 980) to one 'Reactions' tunable.
- Keep today's values, so nothing changes. Moving _HELD_BLEND_S and _GRAB_EASE_S the same way is optional.
- Parts (a), (b) and (c) belong to r2-dummy-comeback, and part (e) to r2-vfx-first-use.

TUNING: new values go in Ragdoll > 'Hips spring' or 'Knocked off the feet (full)', in 'Grab and weapons' (above the 'Hold view' subgroup), and in 'Reactions' right after getup_invuln_frames. r2-dummy-comeback adds its values after dummy_revive_s.
ARCHITECTURE: only the Ragdoll paragraph's Partial/Full bullet, its 'Following the sim' bullet and its 'Get-up' bullet. r2-dummy-comeback edits the 'KO and blink-off' bullet.

RECORD
- Copy the gap reviewer's probe (/Users/arachne/repos/beat-em-up-PoC/.worktrees/m2-review-gap/captures/review_gap/gap_probe.gd and gap_probe.tscn) into your own captures folder and fix its paths.
- Run it before and after the fix: --act=W1|W2|W3|W7|W8|W9 (walls, building fronts, curb) and --act=U1 (from behind, lens metrics).
- Record the wall and curb launches in both views and the from-behind uppercut in first person, then LOOK at the sheets.
- ragdoll_bot's --act takes a single title (gap-09, unverified).

RISKS
- Approved behaviour to keep: heavy-tier knockdowns get the full ragdoll; KO bodies lie, blink off and vanish; the contact push with its spin caps. More contortion on the push is open with Game-boy, so don't change the push.
- The launch out of a hold (test_launch_from_hold.gd, the throw's arc, the knee KO) must stay exactly as it is, including the point-blank throw into a wall, which reads fine today.
- A launch in open space must look as it does now: the snap shows through the finisher's hitstop and slow-mo.
- A downed body's hurtboxes must still match the drawn body, so stomps keep landing.

packages.title: First-use hitches (the first comic sprite, the impact frame, the damage-look shader variant) and side-view burst sizes
packages.notes:
PRIORITY 2. Two mediums and a low. perf-01 and hit-05 share the hub files vfx_director.gd and comic_sprite.gd, but not a root cause.

OWNERSHIP
- Owns: game/fx/vfx_director.gd, comic_sprite.gd, impact_frame.gd, damage_look.gd, vfx_art.gd and speed_lines.gd, and tests/test_vfx.gd.
- humanoid_rig.gd: ONLY _build_materials(), set_damage_look() and the flash_at() doc comment. r2-launch-into-walls owns the Ragdoll block; r2-player-ko-view owns _apply_layers() and the first_person_body export.
- Don't touch the contact flash's code (hit_flash.gdshader, the flash_at() code, _warm_flash()) or test_hit_flash.gd.

ORDER
1) perf-01.
- Warm VfxDirector's first-use materials at load, the way HumanoidRig._warm_flash() warms the flash overlay. Do it only with a window and skip it headless, so the GUT run is unchanged.
- Once the director is in a windowed tree, show one ComicSprite of each material combination it uses (POP with no_depth_test, THROWN, LYING shaded) for one frame, tiny and inside the camera frustum, then retire it to the pool.
- Draw the ImpactFrame's material once: a 1 px rect for one frame, or flash(0).
- Nothing may be visible at load: no ink frame, no burst.
- Test in test_vfx.gd that the warm-up runs with a window and is skipped headless.
- Measure with the perf reviewer's probe: copy /Users/arachne/repos/beat-em-up-PoC/.worktrees/m2-review-perf/captures/review_perf/probe_finisher.tscn (and its script) plus vs.py into your captures folder. A fresh run's first hit should go from a 24-38 ms frame to about 18-23 ms (3-4 ms of CPU), and the first finisher's canvas pipeline compile should be gone.
2) perf-02.
- Never switch the material's shader variant. In _build_materials(), keep detail_enabled, MIX blending, detail UV1 and uv1_triplanar on for the bruisable paints.
- A fully transparent detail texture stands for CLEAN (for example a 1x1 texture VfxArt holds for the run). DamageLook.apply() then swaps only detail_albedo and uv1_scale, the way set_flash() keeps emission on.
- CLEAN must look exactly as it does now.
- Tests: a damage-look change leaves the material's shader RID unchanged, and CLEAN, BRUISED and BLOODIED still pick the same textures.
- Measure with probe_look.tscn from the same folder: a bruise with no other body bruised should go from 3-5 ms to 0.1-0.4 ms, with no surface pipeline compile.
3) hit-05.
- In side view the per-kind floor (ComicSprite.size_factor(): vfx_min_view_share x view_w / the kind's smallest member) blows the large tiers up 2-2.5x.
- Limit the larger tiers' growth when the floor binds. For example, the floor lifts the smallest member to the share and the others by less, or a growth cap as a new tunable in VFX > 'Size and view'. You can also move the heavy word further from the contact in screen space, so the head shows.
- Keep SPEC §6's three distinct burst sizes in order (small, medium, large), the light burst's 4% floor, and every first-person size exactly as it is now. Test both in test_vfx.gd at first-person and side-view distances.
- Re-record in side view: ragdoll_bot's guard-break stagger and hook, and vfx_bot's 'P P P P (side view)'. The guard break's arms, the hook's head rocking back and the launched upper body must show.
4) gap-08, part (e) only.
- In the flash_at() doc comment, change '3 m' to 'about 4' (tuning_data.gd:131 and ARCHITECTURE say about 4).
- Optional: the stale comment at speed_lines.gd:26-27.
- Parts (a) to (d) belong to the other packages.

TUNING: only VFX > 'Size and view'.
ARCHITECTURE: only the 'VFX' paragraph under 'Interfaces between modules': the warm-up, the always-on detail layer, and the side-view sizing rule. That paragraph says today that the tiers keep their ratios at any distance, so update it.

RISKS
- The side-view flash's minimum on-screen size is open with Game-boy (default: leave it). Don't enlarge the flash or give it a floor. Smaller bursts will show more of it, so record the haymaker finisher in side view for the lead.
- The flurry strobe and the flash's first-person size (hit-01, grab-05) are open: leave the contact flash alone.
- WP2 replaced a per-sprite clamp because it made the bursts the same size (HANDOFF). Keep the tiers visibly different.
- The warm-up must not change the photosensitivity toggle: with impact_frame_enabled off, no ink frame ever shows.

packages.title: The player's own KO and get-up in first person, and the player's shins over the lying body on a stomp
packages.notes:
PRIORITY 3. One medium and one low.

OWNERSHIP
- Owns: game/player/player.gd, game/camera/first_person_camera.gd, game/actors/placeholder_body.gd, tests/test_grab_view.gd, tests/test_combat_integration.gd and tests/fp_view.gd. In fp_view.gd, add helpers only and keep the existing ones as they are.
- humanoid_rig.gd: ONLY _apply_layers() and the first_person_body export (add a setter or an export beside it). The other packages own the Ragdoll block, and _build_materials(), set_damage_look() and flash_at().
- Don't edit combat_actor.gd (r2-launch-into-walls) or training_dummy.gd. Read the player's state through the existing public API.

ORDER
1) gap-02.
- Today: the player never ragdolls (ragdoll_player is off) and never blinks off. While it is KO'd, the lens rides the sinking EyePoint 7 cm above the floor, behind the player's own navy belly (41% of the view), for 2.5 s. On the get-up the lens comes within 1.7 cm of its own mesh.
- Fix it in presentation only. While the player is KO'd or getting up, put its own torso, hips and legs on VIS_FP_HIDDEN. Put them back on the default layer the moment it stands, so the normal hide list and test_first_person_body_hides_only_head_neck_chest_and_shoulder_ends don't change.
- Keep the lens on an eased path that never sinks into the body, and tilt it up slightly only if that's needed. Any value goes in a new 'First-person KO view' subgroup at the end of the Camera group.
- This is the reviewer's proposed default. Don't build a KO camera.
- Tests (test_grab_view.gd, or a new file if that reads better), through the real FirstPersonCamera:
  - a KO and get-up while standing: the own body covers at most a third of the view, and nothing is within 0.25 m;
  - the same while holding: the hold view still eases out with no pop, and the released victim still freezes for the hitstop, then staggers away (grab-02).
2) gap-06.
- A skeptic who re-recorded this couldn't see the shins in the hips, so measure first. Use ragdoll_bot's 'Ragdoll: stomp a lying dummy, it gets up where it lies (side view)', and measure the player's shins and feet against the lying body's hurtboxes and drawn mesh through the stand-over (the gap probe's vertex-depth measure).
- If they overlap by more than a few cm, stop the stomp's approach (_stop_distance(), _begin_magnet(), _update_lunge()) clear of the lying body's hips and legs, not only its chest.
- Measure against its hurtboxes, which ride the lying animation, never against its ragdoll. The suggested 'drawn limbs' would make the simulation read the ragdoll (see gap-07).
- Any new number goes in 'Feel details' beside stomp_stop_distance. Test it in test_combat_integration.gd.
- If the overlap isn't real, report no_change_needed with the numbers.

ARCHITECTURE: only the first-person paragraphs: a short 'First-person KO view' paragraph after 'First-person hold view', or a sentence in 'First-person lens'.

RECORD
- Copy the gap probe (/Users/arachne/repos/beat-em-up-PoC/.worktrees/m2-review-gap/captures/review_gap/gap_probe.gd and gap_probe.tscn) into your own captures folder.
- In first person, rerun --act=KO1 and the probe's KO-while-holding act, before and after the fix.
- Record the stomp act in side view.
- LOOK at the sheets.

RISKS AND OPEN QUESTIONS
- What the first-person view shows during the player's KO is new behaviour. The lead must put it to Game-boy at sign-off (the alternative is a short KO camera), so write it in 'remaining'.
- A hit on the player in first person (hit-02) is open with Game-boy. Add no hit or KO feedback: no vignette, no flash on the arms, no new burst.
- Approved: the grab view's pan down with the lens back and up, the knee rising to the right, the player's gray trousers.
- The hold's look dead band and the lens pull-back are open with Game-boy, so leave _tick_hold_view() and the hold-view tunables alone.
- Keep ragdoll-05's fix: the stomp's foot still lands on top of the lying torso, and the stomp still connects.

packages.title: A dummy coming back beside its occupied post; KO and respawn numbers into TuningData; the hook stagger's straight far arm
packages.notes:
PRIORITY 4. All low.

OWNERSHIP
- Owns: game/enemies/dummy/training_dummy.gd, tests/test_ko_blink.gd, and a new tests/test_stagger_pose.gd.
- combat_actor.gd: ONLY blink_shown() (its 0.5 duty and its doc comment). r2-launch-into-walls owns the rest.
- placeholder_poses.gd: ONLY stagger_right_a() and stagger_right_b(). stagger_left mirrors them in placeholder_anims.gd, which you don't edit. r2-launch-into-walls owns launched_a() and launched_b().
- Don't touch _has_room()'s ragdoll read: r2-launch-into-walls fixes the stale read inside Ragdoll.start() (gap-07). Don't edit test_ragdoll.gd or test_humanoid_rig.gd.

MERGED: gap-05 and gap-08's parts (b) and (c) are the same code: the respawn rings and return_home's numbers.

ORDER
1) gap-05, with gap-08 (b) and (c).
- In _respawn_spot(): space the rings with a clearance (2 body radii plus a new gap tunable), so ring 1 no longer touches a player standing on the post.
- Break ties among equally far spots toward the player's view: in front of him or beside him, never behind. Use the player's facing or look from the simulation, never a camera.
- In _tick_control()'s return_home branch: don't walk home while the post has no room (_has_room(_home) is false), and stop walking when the walk makes no progress, instead of striding in place against the player.
- Move return_home's 60 idle frames, its 0.3 m slack, its 6.0 turn rate and the ring gap into TuningData's 'Reactions' group, right after dummy_revive_s. Keep today's values except the new gap. The sparring walk's 4.0 turn rate (line 225) can move too (optional).
- Tests in test_ko_blink.gd: with the player on the post, the dummy comes back clear of him and in his view, and never pushes into him or walks in place. With the post free, it still comes back on the post.
2) gap-08 (a).
- blink_shown()'s 50% on/off duty becomes a ko_blink_duty tunable (0.5) in Ragdoll > 'KO and blink-off', after ko_blink_in_hz.
- The default is the same, so test_ko_blink.gd still passes unchanged.
3) gap-04.
- The hook's far arm swings out nearly straight (about 70 degrees, the elbow barely bent) for about 0.25 s, because stagger_right_a() and stagger_right_b() pose it that way. The arm influence can't calm a swing that is in the animation.
- Re-pose that arm: bent near the guard, no more than about 45 degrees out from the trunk. Keep a visible fling and the trunk's rock-back (ragdoll-02).
- Add a drawn-arm check in tests/test_stagger_pose.gd: the far hand's distance from the trunk in the drawn pose.
- Re-record with and without --no-ragdoll: the hook in first person, and the hook, push-kick and release staggers in side view.
- One skeptic judged the fling intentional (the poses are documented as 'arms out' and 'flung'). If the re-pose makes the stagger read worse from the side, keep the fling and report it in 'remaining' with both sheets. The lead then takes it to Game-boy.

ARCHITECTURE: only the Ragdoll paragraph's 'KO and blink-off' bullet and its 'Someone on the post' sub-bullet. r2-launch-into-walls edits the Partial/Full, 'Following the sim' and 'Get-up' bullets. gap-04 needs no ARCHITECTURE edit.

RECORD
- Copy the gap probe (/Users/arachne/repos/beat-em-up-PoC/.worktrees/m2-review-gap/captures/review_gap/gap_probe.gd and gap_probe.tscn) into your own captures folder.
- Run --act=K3 (the respawn beside the occupied post, side view) before and after the fix, and also look at the comeback in first person.
- ragdoll_bot's --act takes a single title (gap-09, unverified).

RISKS
- Approved: dummies blink back in at their post. ARCHITECTURE and the Decisions log also say the dummy comes back at 'the nearest free spot one or two body widths around it; with none it waits'. Keep the spot within about two body widths. Choosing a spot in view is an implementation choice the docs don't cover.
- Keep code-02's and code-04's fixes: lying bodies, walls, floor, ghosts, same-tick double picks, and the ghost until the blink-in ends. Simultaneous KOs must still come back together.
- The staggers at 0.9 influence are approved: don't change the ragdoll_partial_* tunables.
- Old presets keep their defaults for missing keys, so no PRESET_FORMAT bump is needed.

unassigned.reason: Not verified yet: verify-gap.json lists gap-09 as pending, with no skeptic verdict, so it can't be partitioned under the survives-and-not-a-spec-question rule. It is a bot-harness fix: ragdoll_bot._run filters with contains() instead of the inherited _matches(), so --act=a|b runs no act; combo_bot parks unused dummies at z -30, off the ground box, where they fall forever. It touches only tests/bot/ragdoll_bot.gd and tests/bot/combo_bot.gd, which no package owns. Once it is verified, the lead can fix it directly or add it to r2-dummy-comeback. Until then, fixers pass one act title per ragdoll_bot run.
